frs_sections.title: SCOPE AND MOTIVATION
frs_sections.content:
================================================================================
Standard enterprise Ethernet (10/100/1000BASE-T over Cat-5/Cat-6) uses FOUR
twisted pairs (or, at 100BASE-TX, two pairs with multi-level MLT-3, and at
1000BASE-T, all four pairs bidirectionally). Optical and backplane Ethernet
use 8b10b or 64b/66b line codes over multiple lanes. None of these fit the
automotive harness, where weight, cost, and connector count must be minimised.

Automotive Ethernet therefore defines a family of PHYs that run full Ethernet
over ONE single unshielded twisted pair (one balanced pair, UTP). The single
pair carries traffic in BOTH directions AT THE SAME TIME (simultaneous
bidirectional / full-duplex), separated by echo cancellation. This is the
defining structural property of the T…

frs_sections.title: PHY VARIANTS
frs_sections.content:
================================================================================

2.1 100BASE-T1 (IEEE 802.3bw-2015; formerly OPEN Alliance BroadR-Reach)
    Data rate ........... 100 Mb/s
    Pairs ............... ONE single unshielded twisted pair
    Direction ........... simultaneous bidirectional (full-duplex) on the one
                          pair, separated by ECHO CANCELLATION
    Line modulation ..... PAM3 (3-level: -1, 0, +1; ternary)
    Symbol/baud rate .... 66.67 MBd (66 2/3 MBd)
    PCS coding .......... 4B3B then 3B2T mapping with a side-stream scrambler
                          (maps 4 data bits to 3 ternary symbols)
    Reach ............... up to ~15 m (automotive in-vehicle link segment)
    Timing .............. PHY-level master/slave (one end is the timing master)

frs_sections.title: PHY-LEVEL MASTER / SLAVE TIMING
frs_sections.content:
================================================================================
One PHY end is the timing MASTER, the other the timing SLAVE:
    MASTER : sources the transmit symbol clock from its local reference;
             its scrambler uses the master seed.
    SLAVE  : recovers the symbol clock from the received signal (loop-timed),
             uses the slave scrambler seed.
The master/slave role is fixed per link by configuration (or resolved by
auto-negotiation / OPEN-Alliance link-up). The roles MUST be opposite at the
two ends or the link will not train. (For 10BASE-T1S multidrop, PLCA node 0
is the coordinator.)

================================================================================

frs_sections.title: LINK TRAINING / STARTUP
frs_sections.content:
================================================================================
PHY startup sequence:
    1. Power-on / reset.
    2. Master/slave roles applied (config or auto-negotiation).
    3. PMA link training: the slave acquires symbol timing from the master;
       the adaptive equaliser (FFE/DFE) and the ECHO CANCELLER converge; SNR
       and MSE (mean-squared error) are driven below the link threshold.
    4. PCS achieves descrambler lock and alignment.
    5. PHY reports link-up (link_status = OK); the MAC begins frame exchange.
SNR and MSE are the principal training/health metrics; a PHY that cannot drive
MSE below threshold within the training timer reports a training failure and
the link stays down.

frs_sections.title: SNR / MSE LINK QUALITY
frs_sections.content:
================================================================================
Link quality is monitored via:
    SNR  : signal-to-noise ratio at the slicer.
    MSE  : mean-squared error of the equaliser/slicer (the residual error
           after echo cancellation + equalisation). MSE below a configured
           threshold is the link-up criterion; rising MSE warns of cable /
           connector / EMC degradation.
These are exposed via PHY management registers (MDIO) for in-system diagnostics
and OPEN-Alliance compliance test (link quality, return loss, EMC).

================================================================================

frs_sections.title: AUTOMOTIVE EMC
frs_sections.content:
================================================================================
Automotive EMC (electromagnetic compatibility) is a first-class requirement:
controlled emissions (the PAM3 ternary signalling + scrambler limit the
spectrum), high immunity (the differential pair + common-mode chokes reject
bulk-current-injection and field coupling), and limited reach to keep coupled
noise bounded. OPEN-Alliance TC publishes the automotive EMC + interoperability
test specifications layered on the IEEE PHY.

frs_sections.title: ERROR / FAULT CONDITIONS
frs_sections.content:
================================================================================
    - Link training failure: MSE cannot be driven below threshold within the
      training timer; link stays down.
    - Master/slave misconfiguration: both ends master (or both slave) — the
      link never trains.
    - Loss of descrambler lock: PCS de-locks; link down.
    - SNR/MSE degradation above threshold: warns of cable/connector/EMC fault.
    - FCS (CRC-32) mismatch: receive MAC discards the frame.
    - Runt (<64 B) / giant (>1518/1522 B) frame: discarded.
    - PLCA (10BASE-T1S): a node transmitting outside its transmit opportunity
      is a PLCA violation; missing beacon recovers to a free-for-all timeout.

================================================================================

frs_sections.content:
================================================================================
    - PMA test modes / transmitter test patterns for emissions + jitter.
    - SNR / MSE readout via MDIO for in-system link-quality monitoring.
    - PLCA status counters (10BASE-T1S).
    - OPEN-Alliance interoperability + EMC compliance test specifications.

    - Master/slave force for channel characterisation.

protocol_overview.type: Single-twisted-pair Automotive-Ethernet PHY family (100BASE-T1 / 1000BASE-T1 / 10BASE-T1S / 10BASE-T1L) layered MAC -> RS (optionally PLCA RS) -> PCS -> PMA -> PMD over ONE balanced twisted pair, with simultaneous-bidirectional full-duplex via echo cancellation and PHY-level master/slave loop timing. The IEEE 802.3 Clause-4 MAC frame format is preserved.
protocol_overview.medium: single unshielded twisted pair (UTP, one balanced pair)
protocol_overview.duplex: full-duplex simultaneous bidirectional on the one pair via echo cancellation (point-to-point); half-duplex PLCA-arbitrated on a 10BASE-T1S multidrop segment
protocol_overview.timing_model: PHY-level master/slave loop timing (one master, one slave)
protocol_overview.encoding: 100BASE-T1: 4B3B + 3B2T mapping to PAM3 ternary symbols with a side-stream scrambler. 1000BASE-T1: 80B/81B scrambled PCS to PAM3. The PCS maps the data stream to ternary symbols and applies the master/slave scrambler seed.
interfaces_in_scope: Clause 4 — IEEE 802.3 Ethernet MAC frame format (PRESERVED)
RS / xMII — Reconciliation Sublayer mapping the MAC to the MII/RGMII/SGMII
PLCA Reconciliation Sublayer (10BASE-T1S multidrop) — deterministic transmit-opportunity arbitration
PMA — echo cancellation, adaptive FFE/DFE equalisation, symbol-timing recovery, link training, master/slave clocking
PMD / MDI — single twisted pair, balanced, with automotive EMC filtering

variants.100BASE-T1: 100 Mb/s, IEEE 802.3bw, PAM3 66.67 MBd, BroadR-Reach origin
variants.10BASE-T1L: 10 Mb/s, IEEE 802.3cg, long-reach (up to 1000 m), point-to-point

compliance_requirements: Mandatory simultaneous-bidirectional full-duplex via echo cancellation (point-to-point variants).
Mandatory IEEE 802.3 Clause-4 MAC frame format preservation (FCS = CRC-32 0x04C11DB7).
Mandatory PLCA (Physical Layer Collision Avoidance) on a 10BASE-T1S multidrop segment.
Per-variant automotive EMC (emissions + immunity) compliance per OPEN-Alliance / OEM test specifications.

functional_requirements.text: Each PHY shall carry IEEE 802.3 Ethernet over a SINGLE unshielded twisted pair (one balanced pair). There is no second/third/fourth pair (unlike standard BASE-T); the one defining T1 property is single-pair operation.

Full-duplex operation shall be achieved by SIMULTANEOUS BIDIRECTIONAL transmission on the one pair, separated by an adaptive ECHO CANCELLER that subtracts each PHY's near-end transmit echo so the remote signal can be recovered.
The link shall use PHY-level master/slave loop timing: one PHY (master) sources the symbol clock and the other (slave) recovers it. The two ends MUST have opposite roles or the link shall not train.

100BASE-T1 (IEEE 802.3bw, formerly BroadR-Reach) shall transmit 100 Mb/s using PAM3 (3-level ternary -1/0/+1) at a symbol rate of 66.67 MBd, with a 4B3B + 3B2T PCS mapping and a side-stream scrambler.
1000BASE-T1 (IEEE 802.3bp) shall transmit 1 Gb/s using PAM3 at a symbol rate of 750 MBd with an 80B/81B scrambled PCS.

10BASE-T1S (IEEE 802.3cg) shall support a short-reach MULTIDROP segment shared by several PHYs and shall provide PLCA (Physical Layer Collision Avoidance), implemented as a Reconciliation Sublayer, that grants each node a deterministic transmit opportunity in node-ID order so the shared segment is collision-free without CSMA/CD.
10BASE-T1L (IEEE 802.3cg) shall support a 10 Mb/s long-reach (up to 1000 m) point-to-point single-pair link using PAM3.

Each PHY shall be layered MAC -> RS (optionally PLCA RS) -> PCS -> PMA -> PMD per IEEE 802.3, and shall PRESERVE the IEEE 802.3 Clause-4 MAC frame format (preamble 7x0x55 + SFD 0xD5 + DA + SA + Type/Length + Payload + Pad + FCS CRC-32 0x04C11DB7).

The PMA shall run link training in which the slave acquires symbol timing from the master and the adaptive equaliser (FFE/DFE) and echo canceller converge, driving SNR up and MSE (mean-squared error) below the link-up threshold within the training timer.
The PHY shall expose SNR and MSE link-quality metrics; MSE below the configured threshold shall be the link-up criterion, and rising MSE shall be reported as cable/connector/EMC degradation.

The PHY shall support Energy Efficient Ethernet (EEE) Low-Power Idle (LPI): on MAC idle it shall enter a low-power state, periodically transmit refresh symbols to keep echo-canceller/equaliser coefficients valid, and wake on demand within a bounded wake time.

The PHY shall meet automotive EMC: controlled emissions (PAM3 + scrambler limit the spectrum) and high immunity (balanced pair + common-mode chokes) per the OPEN-Alliance / OEM automotive EMC test specifications.
Every transmitted frame shall append a 32-bit FCS computed with the IEEE 802.3 CRC-32 polynomial 0x04C11DB7 (init 0xFFFFFFFF, final XOR 0xFFFFFFFF, LSB-first) — UNCHANGED from base Ethernet.

The PHY shall be managed over MDC/MDIO (Clause 22 basic registers + Clause 45 MMD extensions), exposing master/slave configuration, link/training status, SNR/MSE, PLCA control (10BASE-T1S), and EEE control.

error_response_conditions: Link training failure — the slave cannot drive MSE below threshold (or acquire timing) within the training timer; the link stays down.
Master/slave misconfiguration — both ends configured master (or both slave); the link never trains.
Loss of descrambler / PCS lock — the PCS de-locks; the link is reported down.
SNR/MSE degradation above threshold — warns of cable / connector / EMC fault while the link may still be up.
Echo-canceller divergence — the echo canceller fails to converge (e.g. severe reflection); recovery via re-train.
FCS (CRC-32) mismatch — the receive MAC discards the frame and increments an FCS-error counter.
Runt (< 64 B) or giant (> 1518/1522 B) frame — discarded by the receive MAC.
PLCA violation (10BASE-T1S) — a node transmitting outside its transmit opportunity; a missing beacon recovers to a free-for-all timeout.
